insight_title: Hawaii is moving Zolgensma back into MCO capitation on January 1, 2026
why_it_matters: A gene therapy that was treated as exceptional is being normalized into MCO financial responsibility, so access strategy may need to shift from state carve-out monitoring to plan-level capitation and utilization-management engagement.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The DUR minutes state that the ultra high-cost drug Zolgensma for SMA will be carved back to the MCOs effective January 1, 2026 because other high-cost drugs are now marketed and Zolgensma is no longer unique; the actuary factored it into each of the five MCO capitation rates.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 134-148; extracted PDF text did not expose a page marker near this passage.

insight_title: Hawaii finalized a dental controlled-drug edit limiting key opioids to a 3-day supply
drug_or_class: Oxycodone, hydrocodone, codeine and other dental controlled drugs
why_it_matters: The edit is a narrow access barrier in dental claims, not just a broad opioid policy; manufacturers and access teams may miss it if they only monitor pharmacy PDL tables.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The August 2023 DUR minutes say no outliers were found for oxycodone, hydrocodone, or codeine, all limited to a 3-day supply, and that prospective quantity-limit edits for controlled drugs were finalized beginning June 2023.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 122-135; page marker is Page 3 at line 128.

insight_title: Hawaii's Amitiza criteria require five laxative failures and only short renewal blocks
why_it_matters: The access hurdle is not simply diagnosis-based PA; approval depends on documenting multiple conventional therapy trials, a 60-tablet monthly cap, response documentation, and repeated 3-month renewals.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The PA criteria require chronic idiopathic constipation, failure of conventional therapy, age at least 18, no mechanical GI obstruction, documentation of at least five listed therapies, a maximum quantity of 60 tablets per month, initial approval up to 3 months, and up to three additional 3-month authorizations if responding.
validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insight_title: Idaho rations manufacturer access through quarterly Industry Days
why_it_matters: The most direct manufacturer engagement channel is capacity-constrained: one session per company per year, first-come first-served, with agenda materials due two weeks ahead.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Idaho says Industry Days occur the fourth Wednesday of March, June, September, and December; each company may sign up for one Industry Day per calendar year; meetings last up to 25 minutes; sessions are first-come, first-served; and an agenda with topics, objectives, supporting materials, and Medicaid relevance is due at least two weeks prior.
validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insight_title: Illinois keeps all new drugs under prior approval until D&T review, even within an existing PDL class
why_it_matters: Market entry does not create automatic preferred access; manufacturers must plan around a six-month marketplace threshold, a three-week agenda deadline, and a one-appeal-per-year limit.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Illinois says all new drugs require prior approval until the D&T Advisory Board recommends availability without PA; even a new drug in a PDL class needs D&T approval before preferred status; agenda requests are due at least 3 weeks before the meeting; one appeal is allowed per year per product; and a drug must be marketed for 6 months before review.
validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insight_title: Illinois' January 2026 CGRP review split clinical evidence and rebate submissions into separate channels
why_it_matters: The class-review page is a live signal that migraine economics and clinical evidence are being handled in parallel but distinct pathways.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The class review schedule lists CGRP for the January 8, 2026 D&T Advisory Board meeting and directs financial submissions to the supplemental rebate program email while clinical submissions go to the D&T Advisory Board email.

insight_title: Illinois explicitly separates evidence-based D&T recommendations from net economic PDL choices
why_it_matters: A product can survive clinical comparison yet lose on net economics; the public Board process is clinical, while HFS incorporates supplemental rebates and utilization-shift savings.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Illinois states that if safety, effectiveness, and outcomes show no therapeutic advantage, HFS considers net economic impact; the D&T Board bases review and recommendations on evidence-based clinical information, not cost; HFS also cites $82 million in FY2018 supplemental rebates and savings from shifting utilization.
validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insight_title: Indiana bars MCOs from using more restrictive pharmacy criteria than the statewide Medicaid standard
drug_or_class: SUPDL, non-SUPDL, OTC and carved-out drugs
why_it_matters: Indiana's managed care rule is both an access guardrail and a carve-out playbook: it limits MCO restrictiveness while allowing the state to pull drugs from capitation for rebate, PA-alignment, orphan-drug, and solvency reasons.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The rule says MCOs must follow the SUPDL, allow at least a 72-hour emergency supply without PA, may not use more restrictive criteria including quantitative and nonquantitative limits, and that drugs may be delivered outside capitation for clinical or financial reasons including substantial supplemental rebates, PA alignment issues, orphan/orphan-like drugs, capitation waste, reinsurance, disproportionate use, and MCO requests.
validation_note: Verified against local text line 7; source is HTML with no page marker.

insight_title: Iowa gives manufacturers five minutes and rejects data-on-file in P&T public comment
why_it_matters: Iowa's rules reward concise, peer-reviewed clinical and health-economics evidence submitted in advance; marketing material, late evidence, and data-on-file cannot carry the argument.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Iowa requires sign-up in advance for in-person public comment, limits manufacturer speakers and product lines to 5 minutes, requests clinical and health economics data rather than marketing, asks for a one-page product synopsis and referenced data at least one week before the meeting, and says data-on-file or submitted-for-review articles should not be referenced.

insight_title: Iowa's PDL updates bundle brand-over-generic, 15-day, and mandatory 90-day supply controls
drug_or_class: PDL; brands preferred over generics; 15-day initial supply; mandatory 90-day supply
why_it_matters: Formulary changes are not just preferred/non-preferred decisions; brands-over-generics, starter-fill, and maintenance-supply policies can reshape volume and channel strategy at the same time.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The preferred drug list page shows the current PDL and brands preferred over generics effective June 1, 2026, a 15-day initial prescription supply limit list effective January 1, 2026, and a mandatory 90-day supply prescription list.

insight_title: Kansas added Journavx to PA after seeing likely off-label chronic-pain use and narrowed the supply limit to each episode
why_it_matters: The Board's rationale shows how early claims surveillance can harden criteria: chronic-pain diagnosis signals triggered concern, and the final amended criteria clarify the 14-day supply limit per acute pain incident or episode.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Kansas minutes say Journavx was added to the list of agents requiring PA; Vertex requested unrestricted access; the state said most requests were potentially off-label because patients had chronic-pain diagnosis codes or other pain-medication claims; the Board recommended specifying that the 14-day supply limit is per incident or episode.

insight_title: Kansas approved Kebilidi AADC gene therapy PA but scheduled a 2026 revisit after manufacturer objections
why_it_matters: Even for ultra-rare gene therapy, Kansas may approve criteria while leaving a future review window open when manufacturers argue criteria exceed FDA labeling or impose step therapy.
evidence_quote_or_summary: For AADC Deficiency Gene Therapy Agents, Kansas proposed PA criteria to ensure FDA-label appropriate use; PTC Therapeutics requested criteria without step therapy and additional restrictions beyond FDA labeling; the Board requested review at the October 2026 DUR meeting and approved the criteria unanimously.

insight_title: Kansas approved Niemann-Pick C PA while keeping miglustat step therapy on the table until July 2026 review
why_it_matters: For NPC entrants, the near-term barrier is not just diagnosis confirmation; a legacy miglustat step requirement was important enough for manufacturer comment and a scheduled re-review.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Kansas minutes say Aqneursa and Miplyffa PA criteria were proposed for FDA-label appropriate use; IntraBio requested removal of step therapy with miglustat; the Board requested review at the July 2026 DUR meeting and noted the state can defer discussion if there is no utilization.

insight_title: Kentucky gives industry only three minutes per drug manufacturer and a 7-day exception window after P&T recommendations
why_it_matters: Kentucky's process creates a narrow evidence path: industry presentations are brief, written materials are limited to new label/indication/peer-reviewed information, exceptions must be new information, and the Commissioner makes the final determination.
evidence_quote_or_summary: 907 KAR 23:010 limits pharmaceutical industry representatives to 3 minutes per drug per manufacturer plus 2 minutes for questions; requires presentation requests 5 business days before the meeting; requires nonverbal materials 7 business days before the meeting; allows adversely affected parties to submit written exceptions within 7 calendar days; and states the Commissioner considers timely exceptions before final determination.

insight_title: Kentucky's Brinsupri access requires CT-confirmed non-CF bronchiectasis plus exacerbation history and smoking attestation
why_it_matters: The final criteria require objective confirmation and specialist involvement, then segment adult and adolescent exacerbation thresholds differently; this is a concrete adoption barrier for a new pulmonary product.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Kentucky's Commissioner decision lists Brinsupri as Non-PDL, with 6-month initial and 12-month renewal duration. Criteria require non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis confirmed by chest CT, specialist prescribing/consultation, at least 2 exacerbations for adults or at least 1 for ages 12-17, antibiotic-treated exacerbations in the past 12 months, and a current-smoker attestation/counseling condition; quantity limit is 1 tablet per day.

insight_title: Kentucky's Leqembi IQLIK criteria require prior completion of 18 months of IV Leqembi and biomarker/MRI/ApoE documentation
why_it_matters: Subcutaneous follow-on access depends on a documented IV-treatment history and baseline risk workup; the criteria also block combination use with other amyloid beta-directed antibodies.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The P&T recommendations require MCI due to Alzheimer's disease or mild AD dementia, specialist involvement, completion of 18 months of IV Leqembi, prior confirmation of beta-amyloid plaques, baseline MMSE/MoCA/CDR, brain MRI, ApoE e4 genotype testing, no combination with other amyloid beta-directed antibodies, and renewal based on stabilization or slowing of decline; age limit is 50-90 and QL is one syringe per week.

insight_title: Louisiana's managed-care pharmacy public-comment queue exposes imminent medical-drug policy moves across CAR-T, oncology, ophthalmology, HAE, and Zepbound
therapeutic_area: Managed care pharmacy and medical drug policy
drug_or_class: Anti-CD19 CAR-T immunotherapies, Loargys, Rybrevant, Cyramza, Imjudo, Enhertu, ranibizumab products, Soliris, hereditary angioedema, Zepbound
why_it_matters: The public-comment page is a forward-looking access signal for MCO policy adoption before final implementation; the dates identify active intervention windows.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Louisiana states it posts proposed managed care pharmacy and medical drug policies for public comment before adopting, approving, amending, or implementing them. As of the captured page, policies posted May 27, 2026 closed July 11, 2026 for somatostatin analogs/GH receptor antagonists, anti-CD19 CAR-T, and Loargys; policies posted May 7, 2026 closed June 21, 2026 for Rybrevant, Cyramza, Imjudo, Enhertu, Furoscix, Prevymis, rituximab products, ranibizumab products, and Soliris; multiple April 30, 2026 pharmacy policies, including HAE and POS Zepbound, closed June 14, 2026.

insight_title: Maine's PDL trial rules can invalidate samples and may require pill counts or urine drug tests for controlled-substance failures
drug_or_class: Non-preferred drugs; controlled substances; brand/generic step care
why_it_matters: Maine turns trial/failure into a documentation standard: samples, overrides, and individual purchases may not count, and controlled-substance trials can require unusually concrete proof.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Maine's PDL says adequate trials generally require at least two weeks; a trial is not valid if preferred or non-preferred products were readily available by override, individual purchase, samples, etc.; certain controlled-substance trials may require evidence such as random pill counts and random urine drug tests; preferred brands can lose preference when cost-effective generics are available; and non-FDA-approved indications require at least two published, peer-reviewed, non-contradicted, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized studies.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 7-33; page marker is Page 1 of 62 at line 33.

insight_title: Maine's opioid policy ties day supply, MME, diagnosis text, palliative PA, and post-surgical duration together
why_it_matters: The opioid barrier is multi-layered: day supply and MME edits interact with diagnosis documentation and exception pathways, so claims support must address more than simple PA status.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Maine's PDL says opioid prescriptions for acute pain are limited to 7-day supplies, chronic pain to 30-day supplies, and more than 7 days or more than 30 MME/day requires PA; cancer, end-of-life/hospice, palliative care, and HIV/AIDS symptoms are general exceptions, but cancer diagnosis must be written on the prescription and palliative-care exceptions require PA with clinical documentation; post-surgical opiate PAs can be up to 60 days with medical necessity from the surgical provider.

insight_title: Maryland's mental-health carve-out is drug- and age-specific, not a blanket class carve-out
drug_or_class: Clonidine ER, guanfacine ER, Onyda XR, leuprolide acetate, medroxyprogesterone, Emsam, Ingrezza
why_it_matters: Plan responsibility changes by molecule, age, and indication; a brand may be FFS for one subpopulation and MCO responsibility for another, while still being subject to PDL PA and clinical criteria.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Maryland says mental-health formulary drugs are carved out of the MCO pharmacy benefit and payable FFS, but some remain subject to PDL and clinical criteria. Generic clonidine and guanfacine remain MCO responsibility, while extended-release guanfacine and clonidine, plus Onyda XR, are FFS only for recipients ages 6-17; leuprolide acetate and medroxyprogesterone are FFS for certain diagnosed behavioral disorders in adult males but require PA through CAMP; Emsam and Ingrezza are the only FFS drugs in their listed AHFS classes.
validation_note: Verified against local text lines 7-41 and 264-270; extracted PDF text did not expose page markers.

insight_title: Maryland flags new-to-market PDL drugs for PA until review and stacks migraine CGRP step therapy with clinical criteria and quantity limits
drug_or_class: Aimovig, Ajovy, Emgality, Nurtec ODT, Qulipta, Ubrelvy, Vyepti, Zavzpret and triptans
why_it_matters: Maryland's PDL embeds multiple access edits in abbreviated notation; in migraine, CGRP agents can carry step therapy, clinical criteria, and QLs at the same time, while new-to-market PDL products require PA until reviewed.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The PDL states that new-to-market PDL products require PA until reviewed. In the anti-migraine category, Ajovy, Emgality, and Aimovig are marked Step Therapy plus clinical criteria and quantity limits; Nurtec ODT, Qulipta, Reyvow, Ubrelvy, Vyepti, and Zavzpret are marked with clinical criteria and quantity limits; triptans are also quantity-limited.
